description:
GarageReplication is the Schema for the garagereplications API.
It replicates objects between two independent Garage clusters.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description:
GarageReplicationSpec defines the desired state of GarageReplication.

GarageReplication copies objects between two independent Garage clusters
through their S3 APIs, for replication and migration. It is not a backup:
there are no point-in-time snapshots and no restore, and in mode Mirror a
deletion or an overwrite on the source reaches the destination on the next
run. Each run executes one Kubernetes Job per bucket in the
GarageReplication's namespace, so the Jobs need network access to both S3
endpoints. Only objects (and their user metadata) are copied: buckets, keys,
permissions, quotas, website and lifecycle configuration are not. Deleting a
GarageReplication never deletes object data on either side.

buckets.description: Buckets lists the buckets to replicate, keyed by destination bucket.

items.description: ReplicationBucket maps a source bucket to a destination bucket.

destination.description:
Destination is the bucket name (global alias) on the destination
cluster. It is the list key, so destinations are unique.

source.description: Source is the bucket name (global alias) on the source cluster.

destination.description:
Destination is the cluster objects are written to. Its credentials need
read and write permission on the destination buckets. Destination
buckets must already exist: replication never creates buckets. A
destination bucket can be written by only one GarageReplication.

clusterRef.description:
ClusterRef references a GarageCluster (operator-managed or a
management handle). The S3 endpoint and region are resolved from it.
A cross-namespace reference requires a GarageReferenceGrant in the
cluster's namespace that allows kind GarageReplication.

kubeConfigSecretRef.description:
KubeConfigSecretRef is reserved for a future remote Kubernetes client integration.
It is currently rejected by admission because the operator does not use it.

key.description: The key of the secret to select from.  Must be a valid secret key.

name.description:
Name of the referent.
This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is
allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are
almost certainly wrong.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

optional.description: Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined

namespace.description:
Namespace of the GarageCluster. Defaults to the referencing resource's namespace.
Cross-namespace references require a GarageReferenceGrant where supported by
the owning resource. GarageNode and GarageAdminToken reject them.

credentialsSecretRef.description:
CredentialsSecretRef references a Secret in the GarageReplication's
namespace holding an S3 access key. The Secret must opt in: either it
is the Secret generated for a GarageKey, or it carries the label
garage.rajsingh.info/replication-credentials: "true". The access key ID
is sent to the endpoint, so without this opt-in the right to create a
GarageReplication would amount to reading any Secret. The default data
keys match the Secret generated for a GarageKey.

accessKeyIdKey.description: AccessKeyIDKey is the data key holding the access key ID.

name.description: Name of the Secret in the GarageReplication's namespace.

secretAccessKeyKey.description: SecretAccessKeyKey is the data key holding the secret access key.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: accessKeyIdKey and secretAccessKeyKey must be different

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is an S3 endpoint of any Garage cluster, inside or outside
Kubernetes.

caBundleRef.description:
CABundleRef references a ConfigMap holding a PEM CA bundle used, in
addition to the system trust store, to verify the endpoint's TLS
certificate.

key.description: Key of the ConfigMap holding the PEM bundle.

region.description: Region is the Garage s3_region used for request signing.

url.description:
URL of the S3 API: scheme and host (with an optional port) only, e.g.
https://s3.example.com or http://garage.ns.svc:3900. Buckets are
addressed path-style below it, so it has no path, query, fragment or
credentials.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: exactly one of clusterRef or endpoint must be set

failedJobsHistoryLimit.description: FailedJobsHistoryLimit is the number of finished failed Jobs to keep.

mirror.description:
Mirror configures mode Mirror. Required when mode is Mirror and
rejected otherwise.

maxDeletes.description:
MaxDeletes caps the number of destination objects one run may delete
per bucket. Once reached the run stops and fails with reason
MaxDeletesExceeded; deletions done before that point are kept.

mode.description:
Mode controls whether changes on the source can remove data on the
destination.
  - Copy: copy new and changed objects. Source deletions are not
    propagated. Changed objects are overwritten on the destination.
  - Mirror: the destination reflects the source, including deletions,
    capped by mirror.maxDeletes per bucket and run. The first run waits
    for the trigger-sync annotation.

nodeAffinity.description: Describes node affinity scheduling rules for the pod.

preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringEx.description:
The scheduler will prefer to schedule pods to nodes that satisfy
the affinity expressions specified by this field, but it may choose
a node that violates one or more of the expressions. The node that is
most preferred is the one with the greatest sum of weights, i.e.
for each node that meets all of the scheduling requirements (resource
request, requiredDuringScheduling affinity expressions, etc.),
compute a sum by iterating through the elements of this field and adding
"weight" to the sum if the node matches the corresponding matchExpressions; the
node(s) with the highest sum are the most preferred.

items.description:
An empty preferred scheduling term matches all objects with implicit weight 0
(i.e. it's a no-op). A null preferred scheduling term matches no objects (i.e. is also a no-op).

preference.description: A node selector term, associated with the corresponding weight.

matchExpressions.description: A list of node selector requirements by node's labels.

items.description:
A node selector requirement is a selector that contains values, a key, and an operator
that relates the key and values.

key.description: The label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description:
Represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Gt, and Lt.

values.description:
An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. If the operator is Gt or Lt, the values
array must have a single element, which will be interpreted as an integer.
This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

weight.description: Weight associated with matching the corresponding nodeSelectorTerm, in the range 1-100.

requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExe.description:
If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at
scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node.
If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met
at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to an update), the system
may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.

items.description:

A label query over a set of resources, in this case pods.
If it's null, this PodAffinityTerm matches with no Pods.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

items.description:
A label selector requirement is a selector that contains values, a key, and an operator that
relates the key and values.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description:
operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values.description:
values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,

matchLabels.description:
matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

matchLabelKeys.description:
MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys to select which pods will
be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the
incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key in (value)`
to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration
for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming
pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.
The same key is forbidden to exist in both matchLabelKeys and labelSelector.
Also, matchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.

mismatchLabelKeys.description:

be taken into consideration. The keys are used to lookup values from the
incoming pod labels, those key-value labels are merged with `labelSelector` as `key notin (value)`
to select the group of existing pods which pods will be taken into consideration
for the incoming pod's pod (anti) affinity. Keys that don't exist in the incoming
pod labels will be ignored. The default value is empty.
The same key is forbidden to exist in both mismatchLabelKeys and labelSelector.
Also, mismatchLabelKeys cannot be set when labelSelector isn't set.

An empty selector ({}) matches all namespaces.

topologyKey.description:
This pod should be co-located (affinity) or not co-located (anti-affinity) with the pods matching
the labelSelector in the specified namespaces, where co-located is defined as running on a node
whose value of the label with key topologyKey matches that of any node on which any of the
selected pods is running.
Empty topologyKey is not allowed.

weight.description:
weight associated with matching the corresponding podAffinityTerm,
in the range 1-100.

requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExe.description:
If the affinity requirements specified by this field are not met at
scheduling time, the pod will not be scheduled onto the node.
If the affinity requirements specified by this field cease to be met
at some point during pod execution (e.g. due to a pod label update), the
system may or may not try to eventually evict the pod from its node.
When there are multiple elements, the lists of nodes corresponding to each
podAffinityTerm are intersected, i.e. all terms must be satisfied.

items.description:

relative to the given namespace(s)) that this pod should be
co-located (affinity) or not co-located (anti-affinity) with,
where co-located is defined as running on a node whose value of
the label with key <topologyKey> matches that of any node on which
a pod of the set of pods is running

This pod should be co-located (affinity) or not co-located (anti-affinity) with the pods matching
the labelSelector in the specified namespaces, where co-located is defined as running on a node
whose value of the label with key topologyKey matches that of any node on which any of the
selected pods is running.
Empty topologyKey is not allowed.

items.description:
The pod this Toleration is attached to tolerates any taint that matches
the triple <key,value,effect> using the matching operator <operator>.

effect.description:
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects.
When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.

key.description:
Key is the taint key that the toleration applies to. Empty means match all taint keys.
If the key is empty, operator must be Exists; this combination means to match all values and all keys.

operator.description:
Operator represents a key's relationship to the value.
Valid operators are Exists, Equal, Lt, and Gt. Defaults to Equal.
Exists is equivalent to wildcard for value, so that a pod can
tolerate all taints of a particular category.
Lt and Gt perform numeric comparisons (requires feature gate TaintTolerationComparisonOperators).

tolerationSeconds.description:
TolerationSeconds represents the period of time the toleration (which must be
of effect NoExecute, otherwise this field is ignored) tolerates the taint. By default,
it is not set, which means tolerate the taint forever (do not evict). Zero and
negative values will be treated as 0 (evict immediately) by the system.

value.description:
Value is the taint value the toleration matches to.
If the operator is Exists, the value should be empty, otherwise just a regular string.

claims.description:
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims,
that are used by this container.

This field depends on the
DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers.

items.description: ResourceClaim references one entry in PodSpec.ResourceClaims.

name.description:
Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of
the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available
inside a container.

request.description:
Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim.
If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise
only the result of this request.

limits.description:
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

requests.description:
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified,
otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

retry.description: Retry bounds retries and duration of each per-bucket Job.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: ActiveDeadlineSeconds bounds the duration of a per-bucket Job.

backoffLimit.description:
BackoffLimit is the number of Pod retries of a per-bucket Job. Each
retry restarts the bucket's comparison; already copied objects are
skipped.

schedule.description:
Schedule is a cron expression (standard 5-field syntax, descriptors
such as @hourly, optional CRON_TZ= prefix; UTC otherwise). Without a
schedule, runs happen only through the garage.rajsingh.info/trigger-sync
annotation (one-shot mode, e.g. for migrations).

source.description:
Source is the cluster objects are read from. Its credentials only need
read permission on the source buckets.

clusterRef.description:
ClusterRef references a GarageCluster (operator-managed or a
management handle). The S3 endpoint and region are resolved from it.
A cross-namespace reference requires a GarageReferenceGrant in the
cluster's namespace that allows kind GarageReplication.

kubeConfigSecretRef.description:
KubeConfigSecretRef is reserved for a future remote Kubernetes client integration.
It is currently rejected by admission because the operator does not use it.

key.description: The key of the secret to select from.  Must be a valid secret key.

name.description:
Name of the referent.
This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is
allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are
almost certainly wrong.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

optional.description: Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined

namespace.description:
Namespace of the GarageCluster. Defaults to the referencing resource's namespace.
Cross-namespace references require a GarageReferenceGrant where supported by
the owning resource. GarageNode and GarageAdminToken reject them.

credentialsSecretRef.description:
CredentialsSecretRef references a Secret in the GarageReplication's
namespace holding an S3 access key. The Secret must opt in: either it
is the Secret generated for a GarageKey, or it carries the label
garage.rajsingh.info/replication-credentials: "true". The access key ID
is sent to the endpoint, so without this opt-in the right to create a
GarageReplication would amount to reading any Secret. The default data
keys match the Secret generated for a GarageKey.

accessKeyIdKey.description: AccessKeyIDKey is the data key holding the access key ID.

name.description: Name of the Secret in the GarageReplication's namespace.

secretAccessKeyKey.description: SecretAccessKeyKey is the data key holding the secret access key.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: accessKeyIdKey and secretAccessKeyKey must be different

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is an S3 endpoint of any Garage cluster, inside or outside
Kubernetes.

caBundleRef.description:
CABundleRef references a ConfigMap holding a PEM CA bundle used, in
addition to the system trust store, to verify the endpoint's TLS
certificate.

key.description: Key of the ConfigMap holding the PEM bundle.

region.description: Region is the Garage s3_region used for request signing.

url.description:
URL of the S3 API: scheme and host (with an optional port) only, e.g.
https://s3.example.com or http://garage.ns.svc:3900. Buckets are
addressed path-style below it, so it has no path, query, fragment or
credentials.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: exactly one of clusterRef or endpoint must be set

successfulJobsHistoryLimit.description:
SuccessfulJobsHistoryLimit is the number of finished successful Jobs to
keep.

suspend.description:
Suspend stops starting new runs. A run already in progress finishes;
delete its Jobs to stop it immediately.

bandwidthLimit.description:
BandwidthLimit caps the transfer rate of each per-bucket Job in bytes
per second, with an optional K, M, G suffix (e.g. "50M"). Empty means
unlimited.

checkers.description: Checkers is the number of objects compared in parallel per bucket.

concurrency.description: Concurrency is the number of objects transferred in parallel per bucket.

maxConcurrentBuckets.description: MaxConcurrentBuckets is the number of buckets replicated in parallel.

verification.description:
Verification runs a comparison of source and destination after each
successful copy. Check compares sizes and MD5 hashes (size only for
multipart objects without a stored MD5) and fails the run on any
difference.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: mirror must be set if and only if mode is Mirror
a bucket cannot be replicated onto itself: source and destination are the same endpoint
x-kubernetes-validations.rule: !(has(self.source.endpoint) && has(self.destination.endpoint) && self.source.endpoint.url == self.destination.endpoint.url) || self.buckets.all(b, b.source != b.destination)

status.description: GarageReplicationStatus defines the observed state of GarageReplication.

buckets.description: Buckets reports per-bucket results, keyed by destination bucket.

items.description: ReplicationBucketStatus reports the last result for one bucket.

activeJob.description: ActiveJob is the Job currently replicating this bucket.

hold.description:
Hold is set when this bucket must not run again without a person
asking. Scheduled runs skip a held bucket. Only the trigger-sync
annotation releases it; editing the spec does not.

lastError.description: LastError is a fixed reason for a failed LastJob.

lastJob.description: LastJob is the last finished Job recorded for this bucket.

lastResult.description: LastResult is the outcome of LastJob.

lastRunId.description: LastRunID is the run of LastJob.

lastStatistics.description:
LastStatistics are the copy engine's counters for LastJob. Unset when
the engine reported none (e.g. the Pod was killed).

bytes.description: Bytes is the number of bytes written to the destination.

checks.description: Checks is the number of objects compared and found up to date.

deletes.description: Deletes is the number of destination objects deleted (Mirror).

differences.description: Differences is the number of differences found by verification.

elapsedSeconds.description: ElapsedSeconds is the duration of the copy.

errors.description: Errors is the number of errors.

transfers.description: Transfers is the number of objects written to the destination.

lastSuccessfulTime.description: LastSuccessfulTime is when the last successful Job for this bucket finished.

lastVerification.description: LastVerification is the verification outcome when verification ran.

conditions.description:
Conditions: Ready (configuration resolved; reasons include
CredentialsNotAllowed and DestinationConflict), Synced (every bucket
succeeded in the last run on the current configuration), Suspended.

items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource.

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

currentRun.description: CurrentRun describes the run in progress.

buckets.description: Buckets lists the destination buckets taking part in the run.

completionTime.description: CompletionTime is when the run finished.

id.description: ID identifies the run; it is part of the Job names.

reason.description: Reason is why the run started.

result.description: Result is Succeeded when every bucket of the run succeeded, else Failed.

specHash.description: SpecHash identifies the configuration the run started with.

startTime.description: StartTime is when the run started.

trigger.description: Trigger is the trigger-sync annotation value that started the run.

lastOperation.description: LastOperation records the outcome of the last trigger-sync annotation.

error.description: Error contains the error message when Succeeded is false

succeeded.description: Succeeded indicates the operation completed without error

triggeredAt.description: TriggeredAt is when the operation was triggered

lastRun.description: LastRun describes the most recent finished run.

buckets.description: Buckets lists the destination buckets taking part in the run.

completionTime.description: CompletionTime is when the run finished.

id.description: ID identifies the run; it is part of the Job names.

reason.description: Reason is why the run started.

result.description: Result is Succeeded when every bucket of the run succeeded, else Failed.

specHash.description: SpecHash identifies the configuration the run started with.

startTime.description: StartTime is when the run started.

trigger.description: Trigger is the trigger-sync annotation value that started the run.

lastScheduleTime.description: LastScheduleTime is the start time of the most recent run.

lastSuccessfulSyncTime.description:
LastSuccessfulSyncTime is when the most recent run in which every
bucket succeeded finished.

lastSyncTime.description: LastSyncTime is when the most recent run finished, whatever its result.

nextSyncTime.description:
NextSyncTime is when the next scheduled run starts. Unset without a
schedule or while suspended.

observedGeneration.description: ObservedGeneration is the last observed generation.
